recommendations: Sprint 3 must implement atomic apply, resume, replay, and recertification under the state-writer lock without weakening historical integrity.

beforeClose.title: Canonical Debt Contract and Legacy Remediation
beforeClose.objective: Reconcile Kyro and Lens debt input semantics and deliver a typed append-only canonicalization path that repairs and recertifies closed legacy scopes without changing immutable history.
successCriteria: Kyro and Lens classify every canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, and unsupported debt fixture identically.
An operator can prepare, preview, and atomically canonicalize the motivating legacy debt without manually calculating digests or editing managed files.
A successful repair changes only the targeted live debt and appended provenance while every historical artifact and commitment remains byte-identical.
Doctor, status, recertification, and Lens independently agree that a valid corrected scope is remediated or recertified and reject every forged, stale, partial, or unsupported variant.
The faithful original-incident scenario passes through the isolated package and projected runtime before publication.

requirements.statement: Kyro and Lens must distinguish canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, and unsupported raw debts using the same observable contract.
requirements.rationale: Raw compatibility and canonical output are different responsibilities. Shared golden vectors, including the original D1 variants, must prove identical classification and canonical projection so the output interface is never again mistaken for the input schema.

requirements.statement: All new debt writes and successful remediations must emit exactly the seven-field canonical debt representation.
requirements.rationale: The canonical key set is id, title, origin, priority, status, targetSprint, and note. Exact output prevents hybrid legacy shapes while compatibility readers remain able to diagnose old input.

requirements.statement: A new versioned debt canonicalization operation must bind the complete observed debt and produce an explicit exact canonical after-image.
requirements.rationale: The existing origin-only operation cannot repair the motivating scope. A closed debt.canonicalize operation must preserve identity fields, require explicit canonical values, retire legacy-only keys, use a whole-debt SHA-256 precondition, and resolve multiple field issues atomically without becoming a generic patch.

requirements.statement: Preparation and preview must be read-only, derive all technical digests, expose evidence and unresolved decisions, and never treat suggested values as operator authorization.
requirements.rationale: Origin has strong addedSprint evidence, while priority and target sprint remain business judgments. INPUT_REQUIRED must name every unresolved value, and a complete manifest must be producible without hand-editing managed state or manually calculating hashes.

requirements.statement: Canonicalization apply and resume must remain atomic, append-only, idempotent, and history-preserving under the state-writer lock.
requirements.rationale: Checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, ledger commitment, task, verdict, unrelated debt, and existing provenance bytes are immutable. Stale full-debt state, interruption, or post-write mismatch must produce no competing applied record and must preserve deterministic PREPARED resume.

requirements.statement: Doctor, status, replay, and recertification must support existing and new remediation versions without weakening historical integrity or tamper detection.
requirements.rationale: The new operation requires an explicit protocol revision so old readers fail closed as unsupported. New readers must replay v1, v2, new, and mixed chains; historical schema notes must never short-circuit artifact digest checks; C-NNN must bind the current head.

requirements.statement: Lens must independently verify and render legacy classification, canonicalization provenance, remediation state, and recertification state.
requirements.rationale: Lens is a read-only verifier, not a consumer of Kyro's claimed label. It must recompute commitments and result state, render selected values and retired legacy keys, and show actionable diagnostics with no stale-state fallback.

requirements.statement: A faithful original-incident fixture and a temporary-copy probe of the actual local scope must gate the packaged and installed release.
requirements.rationale: Synthetic canonical fixtures missed the contradiction. Sentinel assertions must preserve the string origin and missing-field shapes; the full before, prepare, preview, apply, Doctor, recertify, and Lens flow must pass with unchanged historical hashes through an isolated package and projected runtime.

requirements.statement: Release documentation must state the Kyro 4.43.5 limitation, compatible upgrade order, operator workflow, and exact certification boundary.
requirements.rationale: Users must not be told that origin-only remediation repairs record-level legacy drift. Documentation must separate local/source success from package, installed-runtime, Lens, and publication evidence.

nonGoals: Rewrite or replace historical checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, or ledger evidence.
Introduce generic JSON Patch or arbitrary path mutation.
Infer priority, target sprint, origin, or note semantics without explicit operator authorization.
Recover missing or corrupted checkpoint bytes from backup or Git.
Canonicalize tasks, verdicts, ADRs, conventions, or non-debt SprintFile structures.
Mutate every legacy scope automatically during installation or Doctor.
Retain legacy-only debt keys in the corrected live canonical object.
Break or rewrite existing v1 or v2 remediation and certification records.
Modify, stage, or commit files in the original Aliva checkout during release validation.
Claim production readiness beyond the covered debt compatibility and append-only remediation contract.

conventions.rule: Never rewrite committed checkpoints, snapshots, narratives, or ledger commitments; remediation may only append provenance and replace the live canonical projection.
Treat inferred legacy values as suggestions only; apply requires explicit operator-supplied canonical values in the manifest.
Every raw-debt classification or canonical projection change must update and pass the shared Kyro and Lens golden vectors.
Do not claim the incident fixed until the faithful legacy fixture passes source, isolated package, projected runtime, Doctor, recertification, and Lens gates.
Probe the actual Aliva scope only through read-only inspection and a temporary copy; never mutate, stage, or commit its checkout during Kyro release validation.

adrs.title: Separate raw debt compatibility from canonical debt output
adrs.context: The incident recurred because Kyro treated the strict Debt output interface as the raw input contract while Lens intentionally normalizes legacy input.
adrs.decision: Classify raw debt as canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, or unsupported, and preserve an exact seven-field canonical output contract for all new writes.
consequences: Doctor and Lens can understand legacy data without calling it canonical, and writers remain strict.
Shared behavior vectors become a compatibility contract across repositories.
alternatives: Use one strict schema for both input and output.
Allow Lens-only defaults without a Kyro classification.

adrs.title: Canonicalize legacy debt as one typed record-level operation
adrs.context: The existing debt.origin.set operation cannot add missing canonical fields or retire legacy-only keys, so strict post-state validation makes the motivating scope unrecoverable.
adrs.decision: Introduce a closed debt.canonicalize operation with a whole-debt digest precondition, preserved identity fields, explicit canonical values, and an exact seven-key after-image.
consequences: One atomic R-NNN resolves all related field issues without intermediate hybrid states.
Routine isolated edits remain owned by normal debt commands rather than remediation.
alternatives: Add independent setters for every debt field.
Expose generic JSON Patch or JSON Pointer mutations.

adrs.title: Version the canonicalization operation as a new protocol revision
adrs.context: Existing Kyro and Lens readers know only the current remediation versions and debt.origin.set semantics.
adrs.decision: Publish debt.canonicalize in a new explicit remediation protocol revision with version-aware replay and mixed-chain coverage.
consequences: Older readers fail closed as unsupported instead of interpreting a known version differently.
New readers must preserve byte-compatible verification of every existing v1 and v2 chain.
alternatives: Add the new operation silently to an existing schema version.
Drop replay support for older remediation records.

adrs.title: Require explicit semantic authority and retire live legacy keys
adrs.context: AddedSprint supports an origin suggestion, but priority and target sprint are business decisions; retaining detail, resolution, or addedSprint would leave a hybrid live contract.
adrs.decision: Preparation may suggest values with evidence, but apply requires explicit operator values and emits exactly the seven canonical debt keys while preserving old bytes only through immutable history and remediation provenance.
consequences: The record distinguishes observed evidence from operator judgment.
Legacy-only keys disappear from live state without erasing historical proof.
alternatives: Silently adopt Lens defaults as historical truth.
Keep legacy-only keys alongside canonical fields.

adrs.title: Gate release on the motivating artifact shape
adrs.context: Synthetic fixtures with otherwise canonical debt allowed the previous implementation to pass while the real model-catalog-and-routing scope remained impossible to remediate.
adrs.decision: Require a faithful minimized fixture plus a temporary-copy probe of the actual scope through source, isolated package, projected runtime, Doctor, recertification, and Lens before publication.
consequences: Fixture sentinel assertions prevent future cleanup from deleting the failure shape.
The original Aliva checkout remains read-only throughout certification.
alternatives: Certify only generated canonical fixtures.
Apply the candidate directly to the original project checkout.

roadmap.sizingRationale: Five sprints follow the dependency chain and isolate independent failure domains. Sprint 1 freezes the raw/canonical contract and faithful reproduction before writers depend on it. Sprint 2 adds the versioned typed operation and operator preparation under the existing transaction model. Sprint 3 proves replay, Doctor, status, and recertification integrity across old, new, and mixed chains. Sprint 4 updates Lens as an independent cross-repository verifier only after Kyro's protocol stabilizes. Sprint 5 certifies the faithful original incident through packaging, projected runtime, Lens, and documentation. Fewer sprints would let writer, verifier, consumer, or release evidence falsely certify one another; more would split cohesive gates without reducing risk. The plan's acceptance matrix is allocated to the relevant sprint as Given/When/Then scenarios during per-sprint planning.

evidence.summary: Added remediation protocol revision 3 and the closed debt.canonicalize operation. The revision is explicit rather than a silent v2 extension (ADR-0003), and CURRENT_SCOPE_REMEDIATION_SCHEMA_VERSION deliberately stays at v2 so nothing yet writes a v3 record and the debt.origin.set flow emits exactly what it did. OPERATION_KINDS_BY_REVISION binds each kind to the revision that introduced it, so a v1/v2 record or manifest carrying debt.canonicalize is rejected rather than reinterpreted, while a v3 record still carries debt.origin.set unchanged. The operation is record-level and closed: one debtId, a precondition digest over the COMPLETE observed debt[] collection, an explicit retiredKeys list, and an after-image validated to exactly the seven canonical keys with valid literals and identity matching debtId. verifyCanonicalizePreconditions is a pure read-only check against observed state: stale collection digest, missing debt, title/status drift, an unlisted surviving legacy key, or retiring a key the record does not carry all fail closed. Application is deliberately absent: the executor returns the new UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION error instead of half-applying.

evidence.summary: Added src/cli/remediation/canonicalize-plan.ts, a pure total planner that consumes assessRawDebt output plus explicit operator decisions and returns READY, INPUT_REQUIRED or NOT_APPLICABLE. It keeps three things apart by construction: observed facts (id, title, status and any already-valid canonical value are carried through unchanged), evidence (addedSprint for a broken origin, the compatibility-composed note for an absent one — offered as suggested, never adopted), and decisions (the only thing that resolves an unsettled field). priority and targetSprint carry no evidence at all, because no observation implies a business judgment. A decision aimed at an already-canonical field is refused as NOT_NEGOTIABLE rather than silently applied, so canonicalization cannot smuggle a content edit; an invalid supplied value is REJECTED rather than coerced. READY emits one record-level operation binding the whole-collection digest, preserving identity and lifecycle, retiring legacy keys only in the proposed after-image, with exactly the seven canonical keys. Added debtCollectionDigest to canonical-state.ts.

evidence.summary: Exposed the planner as read-only preparation and preview on both surfaces, backed by one shared module (src/cli/remediation/canonicalize-surface.ts) so CLI and MCP cannot drift into different answers. CLI: kyro remediate canonicalize-prepare --debt <id> [--origin|--priority|--target-sprint|--note] and kyro remediate canonicalize-preview --manifest <path>. MCP: remediate_canonicalize_prepare and remediate_canonicalize_preview, both annotated readOnlyHint. Decisions are opt-in per field on both surfaces — an omitted flag or argument means undecided, never adopt the suggestion — and target_sprint_null exists because an explicit null is a decision that must be distinguishable from silence. Prepare renders classification, observed values, undecided fields with their evidence, and the whole-debt digest; it returns a complete v3 manifest only when every value is settled, and never saves it. Preview re-checks a held manifest against live state, showing the exact after-image only when the manifest is complete and still true, and exiting non-zero otherwise. Help and the tool catalog describe both as read-only and state plainly that no canonicalize-apply verb exists.

Stale full-debt state, interruption, or post-write mismatch must produce no competing applied record and must preserve deterministic PREPARED resume.

requirements.statement: Doctor, status, replay, and recertification must support existing and new remediation versions without weakening historical integrity or tamper detection.
requirements.rationale: The new operation requires an explicit protocol revision so old readers fail closed as unsupported. New readers must replay v1, v2, new, and mixed chains; historical schema notes must never short-circuit artifact digest checks; C-NNN must bind the current head.

requirements.statement: Lens must independently verify and render legacy classification, canonicalization provenance, remediation state, and recertification state.
requirements.rationale: Lens is a read-only verifier, not a consumer of Kyro's claimed label. It must recompute commitments and result state, render selected values and retired legacy keys, and show actionable diagnostics with no stale-state fallback.

requirements.statement: A faithful original-incident fixture and a temporary-copy probe of the actual local scope must gate the packaged and installed release.
requirements.rationale: Synthetic canonical fixtures missed the contradiction. Sentinel assertions must preserve the string origin and missing-field shapes; the full before, prepare, preview, apply, Doctor, recertify, and Lens flow must pass with unchanged historical hashes through an isolated package and projected runtime.

requirements.statement: Release documentation must state the Kyro 4.43.5 limitation, compatible upgrade order, operator workflow, and exact certification boundary.
requirements.rationale: Users must not be told that origin-only remediation repairs record-level legacy drift. Documentation must separate local/source success from package, installed-runtime, Lens, and publication evidence.

scenarios.then: Both accept it and produce the same canonical values without a legacy diagnostic

scenarios.when: Kyro and Lens evaluate the debt contract
scenarios.then: Both treat it as readable legacy input and derive the same explicit canonical projection without calling the raw object canonical

scenarios.given: The motivating legacy D1 shape with a present string origin
scenarios.when: Kyro and Lens evaluate the debt contract
scenarios.then: Both reject the present invalid origin and Kyro classifies the object as remediation-required with the exact field path

scenarios.when: Kyro and Lens evaluate the debt contract
scenarios.then: Both fail closed without fabricating a trusted canonical projection

scenarios.then: The persisted debt contains exactly id, title, origin, priority, status, targetSprint, and note with valid values

scenarios.when: The faithful fixture and Doctor gates run
scenarios.then: The decisive legacy shapes remain present, historical hashes remain untouched, and any fixture cleanup or artifact tampering fails certification

scenarios.then: it binds the complete observed debt digest and emits exactly one record-level debt.canonicalize plan with an exact seven-key after-image.

scenarios.then: the result is read-only INPUT_REQUIRED diagnostics that distinguish evidence from authorization and no manifest or artifact mutation is produced.

nonGoals: Rewrite or replace historical checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, or ledger evidence.
Introduce generic JSON Patch or arbitrary path mutation.
Infer priority, target sprint, origin, or note semantics without explicit operator authorization.
Recover missing or corrupted checkpoint bytes from backup or Git.
Canonicalize tasks, verdicts, ADRs, conventions, or non-debt SprintFile structures.
Mutate every legacy scope automatically during installation or Doctor.
Retain legacy-only debt keys in the corrected live canonical object.
Break or rewrite existing v1 or v2 remediation and certification records.
Modify, stage, or commit files in the original Aliva checkout during release validation.
Claim production readiness beyond the covered debt compatibility and append-only remediation contract.

conventions.rule: Never rewrite committed checkpoints, snapshots, narratives, or ledger commitments; remediation may only append provenance and replace the live canonical projection.
Treat inferred legacy values as suggestions only; apply requires explicit operator-supplied canonical values in the manifest.
Every raw-debt classification or canonical projection change must update and pass the shared Kyro and Lens golden vectors.
Do not claim the incident fixed until the faithful legacy fixture passes source, isolated package, projected runtime, Doctor, recertification, and Lens gates.
Probe the actual Aliva scope only through read-only inspection and a temporary copy; never mutate, stage, or commit its checkout during Kyro release validation.

adrs.title: Separate raw debt compatibility from canonical debt output
adrs.context: The incident recurred because Kyro treated the strict Debt output interface as the raw input contract while Lens intentionally normalizes legacy input.
adrs.decision: Classify raw debt as canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, or unsupported, and preserve an exact seven-field canonical output contract for all new writes.
consequences: Doctor and Lens can understand legacy data without calling it canonical, and writers remain strict.
Shared behavior vectors become a compatibility contract across repositories.
alternatives: Use one strict schema for both input and output.
Allow Lens-only defaults without a Kyro classification.

adrs.title: Canonicalize legacy debt as one typed record-level operation
adrs.context: The existing debt.origin.set operation cannot add missing canonical fields or retire legacy-only keys, so strict post-state validation makes the motivating scope unrecoverable.
adrs.decision: Introduce a closed debt.canonicalize operation with a whole-debt digest precondition, preserved identity fields, explicit canonical values, and an exact seven-key after-image.
consequences: One atomic R-NNN resolves all related field issues without intermediate hybrid states.
Routine isolated edits remain owned by normal debt commands rather than remediation.
alternatives: Add independent setters for every debt field.
Expose generic JSON Patch or JSON Pointer mutations.

adrs.title: Version the canonicalization operation as a new protocol revision
adrs.context: Existing Kyro and Lens readers know only the current remediation versions and debt.origin.set semantics.
adrs.decision: Publish debt.canonicalize in a new explicit remediation protocol revision with version-aware replay and mixed-chain coverage.
consequences: Older readers fail closed as unsupported instead of interpreting a known version differently.
New readers must preserve byte-compatible verification of every existing v1 and v2 chain.
alternatives: Add the new operation silently to an existing schema version.
Drop replay support for older remediation records.

adrs.title: Require explicit semantic authority and retire live legacy keys
adrs.context: AddedSprint supports an origin suggestion, but priority and target sprint are business decisions; retaining detail, resolution, or addedSprint would leave a hybrid live contract.
adrs.decision: Preparation may suggest values with evidence, but apply requires explicit operator values and emits exactly the seven canonical debt keys while preserving old bytes only through immutable history and remediation provenance.
consequences: The record distinguishes observed evidence from operator judgment.
Legacy-only keys disappear from live state without erasing historical proof.
alternatives: Silently adopt Lens defaults as historical truth.
Keep legacy-only keys alongside canonical fields.

adrs.title: Gate release on the motivating artifact shape
adrs.context: Synthetic fixtures with otherwise canonical debt allowed the previous implementation to pass while the real model-catalog-and-routing scope remained impossible to remediate.
adrs.decision: Require a faithful minimized fixture plus a temporary-copy probe of the actual scope through source, isolated package, projected runtime, Doctor, recertification, and Lens before publication.
consequences: Fixture sentinel assertions prevent future cleanup from deleting the failure shape.
The original Aliva checkout remains read-only throughout certification.
alternatives: Certify only generated canonical fixtures.
Apply the candidate directly to the original project checkout.

roadmap.sizingRationale: Five sprints follow the dependency chain and isolate independent failure domains. Sprint 1 freezes the raw/canonical contract and faithful reproduction before writers depend on it. Sprint 2 adds the versioned typed operation and operator preparation under the existing transaction model. Sprint 3 proves replay, Doctor, status, and recertification integrity across old, new, and mixed chains. Sprint 4 updates Lens as an independent cross-repository verifier only after Kyro's protocol stabilizes. Sprint 5 certifies the faithful original incident through packaging, projected runtime, Lens, and documentation. Fewer sprints would let writer, verifier, consumer, or release evidence falsely certify one another; more would split cohesive gates without reducing risk. The plan's acceptance matrix is allocated to the relevant sprint as Given/When/Then scenarios during per-sprint planning.
